The programme map

Ability, dignity and belonging.

Seven connected fields translate the Trust's registered objects into focused, assessable programme pathways.

Framework stage
Projects are initiated according to verified need, available resources, suitable partners and all required approvals. This page describes the Trust's authorised direction, not a promise that every service is currently operating.
01 / LEARN

Education and 100% skill development

Build a complete learning pathway from literacy and academic support to vocational competence, digital ability, employability, research and teacher development.

  • Schools, colleges and polytechnics
  • Vocational and computer training
  • Libraries, laboratories and research centres
  • Scholarship and guidance support
02 / GROW

Child and youth development

Help children and young people learn safely, recover lost opportunities, build confidence and participate in constructive social and physical activities.

  • Pre-school and child-welfare services
  • Support for drop-out and street-connected children
  • Sports, yoga and life skills
  • Drug-abuse prevention and counselling
03 / CARE

Orphan and elder dignity

Create reliable care pathways for children, young people and elders who lack dependable family or community support.

  • Child and elder care-centre models
  • Nutrition, clothing and shelter support
  • Health monitoring and companionship
  • Education or rehabilitation pathways
04 / HEAL

Medical aid and emergency support

Coordinate timely, need-based healthcare support while building longer-term access through camps, dispensary pathways and institutional partnerships.

  • Medical assistance for people in need
  • Medicine and dispensary support
  • Eye, blood-donation and awareness camps
  • Emergency referral and partner coordination
05 / INCLUDE

Different abilities and women's welfare

Advance inclusion, safety, learning and economic independence for persons with physical, sensory, intellectual or developmental disabilities and for women facing social or economic barriers.

  • Special and vocational education
  • Assistive devices and accessibility support
  • Self-employment and sheltered-work pathways
  • Counselling, service homes and self-help groups
06 / BUILD

Rural livelihoods and agricultural development

Connect training, natural-resource knowledge and market access so rural youth and families can build resilient, locally relevant livelihoods.

  • Natural, vertical and precision farming
  • Livestock, dairy, fisheries and beekeeping
  • Nursery, herbs, mushrooms and seed production
  • Small industries, warehousing and market linkage
07 / PROTECT

Environment, animals and community wellbeing

Promote responsible stewardship of shared natural resources alongside practical improvements in living conditions.

  • Forest and tree protection
  • Bird and animal welfare
  • Shelter and sanitation support
  • Traditional food and healthy-living awareness
Delivery discipline

From a genuine need to a responsible response.

Every programme should move through a clear cycle rather than a one-time transaction.

01 · IDENTIFY

Listen locally

Understand the person, community, evidence and root cause before selecting an intervention.

02 · ASSESS

Verify responsibly

Review eligibility, urgency, safeguarding, resources, partners and applicable legal requirements.

03 · ACT

Deliver the right support

Use funds, materials, expertise or referrals in a documented and purpose-aligned manner.

04 · FOLLOW

Measure continuity

Check what changed, what remains at risk and which next step can support lasting progress.

Programme safeguards

Public benefit remains the centre.

The deed requires charitable, non-profit activity within India and makes benefits available to the public without prohibited discrimination.

No profit intentionActivities are carried out for charitable objects.
Purpose-led fundsIncome and funds are used only for the Trust's objects.
Approvals matterInstitutions and specialised services begin only after required permissions.
